name: Aortic arch (great vessel origins)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Same aortic arch that continues as the descending thoracic aorta (data/vascular/trunk_arterial.json's root) -- modeled as a separate tree root here only because of this atlas's per-region file split, not because it is a different anatomical structure. Gives rise, in order, to the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid a., and left subclavian a.

name: Brachiocephalic trunk
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Divides into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries; the left side's equivalents arise directly from the arch instead of via a shared trunk -- an asymmetry this atlas represents with one generic side per vessel (see module docstring).

name: Common carotid artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Ascends in the carotid sheath without branching until it bifurcates at approximately the C3-C4 vertebral level (the carotid bifurcation, marked by the carotid body chemoreceptor and carotid sinus baroreceptor).

name: External carotid artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Supplies essentially all extracranial head & neck structures via its 6 named cervical/facial branches plus 2 terminal branches.

name: Internal carotid artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
supplies_or_drains: brain and orbit contents (intracranial, out of scope for this musculoskeletal-focused atlas)
notes: No branches in the neck; ascends to enter the carotid canal of the temporal bone and become intracranial. Intracranial distribution (supplying the brain) is out of scope, consistent with the organ-parenchyma boundary documented in docs/ROADMAP.md Stage 4 -- modeled here as a leaf/stub.

name: Superior thyroid artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
supplies_or_drains: thyroid gland (out of scope as an organ, noted for completeness)
notes: First and most inferior branch of the external carotid; also supplies the infrahyoid strap muscles' inferior fibers and sternocleidomastoid's anterior border via small muscular twigs.

name: Lingual artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Passes deep to hyoglossus -- a classic anatomical landmark relationship also noted in hyoglossus's own muscle file.

name: Facial artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Tortuous course crossing the mandible's inferior border anterior to masseter (a standard pulse-palpation point), then ascending tortuously alongside the nose to the medial eye.

name: Ascending pharyngeal artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Smallest and most medial branch of the external carotid, the only one without a consistently named terminal territory outside the pharynx/prevertebral region.

name: Occipital artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Runs deep to the posterior belly of digastric, which it crosses; supplies the posterior scalp beyond this atlas's modeled muscle territory too.

name: Posterior auricular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Small branch supplying the region around and behind the ear, and a small contribution to the posterior belly of digastric alongside occipital a.

name: Superficial temporal artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: One of the external carotid's 2 terminal branches; palpable anterior to the ear (a classic pulse point) before dividing into frontal and parietal scalp branches.

name: Maxillary artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: The external carotid's other, larger terminal branch (confirmed larger-caliber than superficial temporal a.); its pterygoid (2nd) part supplies all 4 muscles of mastication via distinct named branches -- the masseteric artery (masseter), deep temporal arteries (temporalis), and the pterygoid branches proper (medial and lateral pterygoids specifically, not a blanket name for all four) -- adjusted from an earlier draft that used 'pterygoid branches' loosely for all four muscles' supply, caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md.

name: Middle meningeal artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
supplies_or_drains: dura mater (out of musculoskeletal scope, included for its clinical significance)
notes: Enters the skull via the foramen spinosum (already a documented landmark on the sphenoid bone in data/skeleton/bones.json); its rupture from a temporal bone fracture is the classic cause of an epidural (extradural) hematoma.

name: Inferior alveolar artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Enters the mandibular foramen (a documented landmark on the mandible bone) alongside the inferior alveolar nerve and vein, giving off the mylohyoid branch just before entering.
